hook: The physicist who led the making of the first atomic bomb, and then warned the world about it.

pages.x: Robert Oppenheimer was born in New York in 1904 to a wealthy family. At 12 he gave a talk to a club of rock collectors, who had not realised from his letters that he was a child.
Studying in Cambridge, unhappy and homesick, he is said to have left an apple laced with chemicals on his tutor's desk. No one ate it, and his parents talked the university out of expelling him.
At Berkeley, from 1929, he built the best school of theoretical physics in America. In 1939 he worked out how a collapsing star could form what we now call a black hole.

In 1942 he was put in charge of the scientists of the secret Manhattan Project. He chose a remote mesa in New Mexico, Los Alamos, where thousands of people worked to build an atomic bomb before Germany could.
On 16 July 1945 the first atomic bomb exploded in the New Mexico desert. Watching, he remembered words from a Hindu scripture: "Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds."
pages.fx: Weeks later atomic bombs destroyed Hiroshima and Nagasaki, killing well over 100,000 people, and Japan surrendered. The nuclear age had begun.

pages.x: After the war he argued for international control of atomic weapons, and opposed building the far more powerful hydrogen bomb. He told President Truman: "I feel I have blood on my hands."

In 1954, in the fear of communism, a government hearing took away his security clearance, over old left-wing friends and his opposition to the hydrogen bomb. In 2022 the American government reversed the decision.
He led the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, where Einstein worked. A heavy smoker, he died of throat cancer in 1967.
Oppenheimer led the making of the first atomic bomb, which ended the Second World War and changed the world for ever, and spent the rest of his life warning of its dangers.
pts: Led the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos
Called the father of the atomic bomb
Warned the world about nuclear weapons
